title: Which of these four sets of lengths make a triangle?
description: Four sets of lengths are tested with the three steps: find the longest, add the other two and compare. One set has an equal sum, where the circles only touch.
teaching_notes: One idea: a triangle needs the sum of the two shorter lengths to be more than the longest, and an equal sum is not enough. Watch for children who accept the set three, six, nine because the circles touch.

source: Check if a triangle exists for each of the following set of lengths: (a) 1, 100, 100 (b) 3, 6, 9 (c) 1, 1, 5 (d) 5, 10, 12
video_script.why: The child has the three steps and the touch, miss or cross cases and now applies them to four sets, one of which is a touching case.
video_script.substitution: In each set the longest length is compared with the other two added together.
video_script.anchor: Four sets of lengths, one to four, to be tested with the three steps
video_script.payoff_line: Triangles exist for the first and fourth sets, but not for the second or third.

final_answer.value: Triangles exist for (a) and (d); not for (b) (circles touch) or (c)
final_answer.spoken: triangles exist for the first and fourth sets, but not for the second, where the circles touch, or the third

never_show: the words triangles exist before the answer beat
maths_rules: check: in (b) the touching place lies on the base, so the three corners are in one line
video_script.design: One idea: a triangle needs the sum of the two shorter lengths to be more than the longest. The four sets stay in the anchor band; the working band holds the board solution.

beats.on_screen: four cards labelled a to d: 1, 100, 100; 3, 6, 9; 1, 1, 5; 5, 10, 12; a question mark
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
Four sets of three lengths are given.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Check if a triangle exists for each set.

beats.on_screen: the four cards and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the card with the three steps: find the longest, add the other two, compare

marks.card: the card with three steps appears
marks.touch: a small picture of touching circles appears beside the card

narration: <bookmark mark='card'/>Use the three steps from the last video.
<bookmark mark='touch'/>Find the longest, add the other two, and compare.

marks.given: the four sets are written in a list

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the four sets, in the order of the book.

beats.on_screen: To find: which sets pass the check?
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which sets pass the check.

marks.a2: 1 + 100 = 101 is written, then 101 > 100 with a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, in the first set the longest length is one hundred.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The other two add to one plus one hundred, which is one hundred and one.
That is more than one hundred, so it passes.

marks.b2: 3 + 6 = 9 is written, then 9 = 9 with a cross

narration: <bookmark mark='b'/>Step two, in the second set the longest length is nine.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>The other two add to three plus six, which is nine.
The sum is equal to the longest, so the circles only touch and it fails.

marks.c2: 1 + 1 = 2 is written, then 2 < 5 with a cross

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step three, in the third set the longest length is five.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>The other two add to one plus one, which is two.
Two is less than five, so it fails.

marks.d2: 5 + 10 = 15 is written, then 15 > 12 with a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='d'/>Step four, in the fourth set the longest length is twelve.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>The other two add to five plus ten, which is fifteen.
Fifteen is more than twelve, so it passes.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check (b): the circles of radii 3 and 6 on a base of 9 touch on the base, so the corners are in one line

marks.check: a base of 9 with circles of radii 3 and 6 is drawn
marks.line: the touching place glows on the base

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the second set with circles.
<bookmark mark='line'/>They touch on the base, so all three corners are in one line.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Triangles exist for (a) and (d); not for (b) (circles touch) or (c)
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Triangles exist for the first and fourth sets, but not for the second or third.
